paths.label: shown
paths.quote: The cast makes it a double division; so you get the decimal part
paths.logic: Values are 64-bit IEEE 754 numbers (about 15 significant digits) plus the special values Infinity and NaN; +, -, *, / (and %) are defined; if at least one operand of a binary arithmetic operator is double, the operation is a floating-point operation.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: 3.5; The cast makes it a double division; so you get the decimal part
paths.logic: With ints, 17 / 3 is 5 and 17 % 3 is 2. With doubles, 5.0 / 3.0 is 1.6666666666666667. With mixed operands, the int is promoted first (10 / 3.0 is 3.333...).

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: The cast makes it a double division; so you get the decimal part
paths.logic: Both operands must be numeric, and the result has the promoted type (int, long or double). * / % bind tighter than + -, all group left to right, and int / or % by zero throws ArithmeticException. Unary minus negates its operand (-x) and unary plus leaves it unchanged; they bind more tightly than * and /, so -a * b is (-a) * b.

paths.label: broken
paths.logic: println("s") outputs exactly the characters between the quotes and then ends the line.
